content: The test image shows corn plants with prominent yellow/white streaking running parallel to the leaf veins — a classic viral symptom pattern. Let me compare reference images for the top candidates.

**Observations from test image:**
- Corn leaves with broad yellow/white streaking running parallel to veins
- Irregular mottled pattern of green and chlorotic areas
- Whole plant affected, multiple leaves show symptoms
- Leaves appear somewhat distorted/twisted

**Comparison with Maize_streak_virus reference:**
- The reference shows very fine, narrow white streaks parallel to veins (bottom-right panel)
- The test image matches this pattern well — longitudinal chlorotic streaking throughout the leaf
- The broader yellowing in the test image is consistent with more advanced/severe streak virus symptoms

The parallel vein streaking pattern throughout the whole plant is the hallmark of Maize streak virus, caused by *Maize streak mastrevirus* (transmitted by leafhoppers). The fine to broad chlorotic streaks running the length of the leaf match perfectly.
